findings.evidence: "Read references/ideation-lenses.md here: run its category coverage check, use its per-scale questions and unstick prompts when candidates run dry, and apply its mindset rules."
findings.fix: Split the load: always read the category coverage check and mindset rules at Discover; load Discovery questions by scale and Prompts to unstick thinking only when the candidate list stalls; load Evaluation lenses only when step 4.2 says two scores are close, and say not to load those sections otherwise.

findings.evidence: casual-strategy, precise-roadmap, feature-request and category-coverage assert "highest-scoring idea" and "cheapest test fits the stated team" with no expected scores, no formula inputs, and no numeric team capacity.
findings.fix: For each of those four evals, add an expected ranking worked from the step 4.2 formula (reach, evidence, effort, adoption cost) plus the capacity the prompt states, so the Do Now assertion is checkable rather than a judgment call.

findings.evidence: "exactly one idea in the session is Do Now, the highest-scoring idea across all tiers whose cheapest test fits the team's stated capacity (ties go to the higher tier)"
findings.fix: State the order when both score and tier tie (for example the cheapest test, then the idea listed first), and say what "fits" means for a stated headcount with no time window (for example a Small-effort test fits, a Large one does not unless the prompt gives a window).
